At the same time, he said, waiting too long for an IPO would be “bad for the world.”

Sam Altman laid out OpenAI's three-step vision for business dominance.

The CEO revealed a slew of updates to ChatGPT and related company products at its developer conference in San Francisco on Tuesday. He also outlined a three-part plan: provide the best AI models, make them the easiest for developers to build on, and become a "marketplace" for business customers to reach one another.

Altman's framing speaks to the vast growth the AI company has seen since it burst into the limelight with ChatGPT — and the pressure that OpenAI and rival Anthropic face to justify their lofty valuations with ambitious business plans.

The first step is "models," then "building," then "distribution," Altman told a crowd of developers and employees at the Fort Mason venue.

"We want to support you all with a powerful platform for building whatever you can dream of," he said.
